observation.visible_scene: An underwater view close to a shallow, sandy seabed. Sunlight refracted through the water surface projects a bright, web-like network of caustic lines across the sand. Above the seabed is a blue water column, and at the top of the frame the rippling water surface with a band of reflected sky. A pale, hazy plume of suspended sediment sits in the mid-water.
visible_changes: The caustic light web on the sand continuously shimmers and deforms from frame to frame: the bright lines bend, merge, and re-form rather than translating as a fixed pattern.
A diffuse, whitish sediment plume in the middle-right of the water column persists and slowly drifts and reshapes throughout the segment.

The water-surface boundary gradually rises within the frame while the bright reflected-sky band at the top widens, consistent with a slow downward tilt of the viewpoint; the seabed caustics come to occupy more of the lower frame.
The rippled texture of the surface itself undulates subtly over time.
outside_clip_unknowns: The origin and later fate of the suspended-sediment plume (whether it disperses, settles, or was stirred up before the crop).
The full magnitude and direction of camera motion before and after this excerpt.
What lies beyond the visible seabed and surface.
uncertain_details: Whether the upward shift of the surface line is due to camera tilt or to a change in water level relative to the lens.
The pink/purple blobs near the top (around t=0.80s) and occasional small bright dots are likely lens flare or surface reflections, not separate physical objects.
The caustic deformation is taken as the visible effect of surface-wave motion; the waves themselves are only partly visible.
